title: FoSA 第 17 章 · 微服务架构：宁可重复，也不要耦合 — 专业书籍精读 Book 224
title_en: FoSA Chapter 17 · Microservices Architecture: Prefer Duplication to Coupling — Book Deep Read 224

questions.question: 好几个微服务都需要一个 Address 地址类。按书中「宁可重复，也不要耦合」的原则，下列哪种复用是书推荐的？
options: 在 API 网关里集中实现地址校验等业务规则，各服务只管调用网关给出的结果
让所有服务共用一个集成数据库，地址数据只存一份，从而彻底避免数据重复
把 Address 这类通用领域类抽成公共库，各服务继承或组合，改一处全局生效
把日志、监控、熔断等运维能力放进 sidecar，再连成服务网格统一管理
questions.explanation: 书的精确修正是：领域逻辑不复用，Address 宁可各写一份；运维关切和领域关切分开，运维能力通过 sidecar 和服务网格复用。共享集成数据库和把业务规则塞进网关，书都明确反对。
questions.question_en: Several microservices need an Address class. Under the book's principle of “prefer duplication to coupling,” which kind of reuse does it recommend?
options_en: Implement business rules such as address validation centrally in the API gateway, with services just calling its results
Have all services share a single integration database so address data is stored once and duplication is eliminated
Extract common domain classes like Address into a shared library every service inherits from, so one change applies everywhere
Put operational capabilities like logging, monitoring, and circuit breaking in sidecars, maintained by a shared team as a service mesh
questions.explanation_en: The book's precise refinement: don't reuse domain logic—duplicate Address in each service—but separate operational from domain concerns and reuse operations via sidecars and a service mesh. It explicitly rejects shared integration databases and business logic in the gateway.

questions.question: 某系统里几乎每个业务动作都要靠 Saga 跨好几个服务协调，并配套大量补偿事务。按书的观点，这首先说明什么？
options: 这是微服务的正常形态，只要补偿事务写成幂等的，就不必再担心
应该把所有服务都改成同步调用，按顺序执行就能避免出现中间状态
服务粒度切错了，总在同一事务里一起改的实体应该合回同一个服务
团队应该引入两阶段提交，用分布式事务重新获得数据库那样的 ACID
questions.explanation: 书说别在微服务里做事务、去修粒度；偶尔几个 Saga 可以接受，常态化就说明边界划错了。把幂等补偿当作解药，忽略了中间态对外可见、补偿本身也可能失败的代价。
questions.question_en: In one system, nearly every business action needs a Saga coordinating several services, with many compensating transactions. What does the book say this indicates first?
options_en: This is normal for microservices; as long as every compensating transaction is idempotent, there's nothing to worry about
All services should switch to synchronous calls; executing in sequence avoids any intermediate states
The service granularity is wrong; entities that always change together in one transaction should be merged into one service
The team should adopt two-phase commit, regaining database-style ACID guarantees through distributed transactions
questions.explanation_en: The book says don't do transactions in microservices—fix the granularity. A few Sagas are acceptable; if they become routine, the boundaries are wrong. Treating idempotent compensation as the cure ignores that intermediate states are visible and compensations can fail.

questions.question: 一个团队把系统拆成十个独立部署的服务，但它们共用同一个数据库，改一张表要所有服务一起协调。按书的说法，这算什么？
options: 一种合理的微服务折中：共享库保证了强一致性，又保留了独立部署的好处
一种事件驱动架构，依靠数据库触发器在这些服务之间传递消息和状态变化
标准的微服务架构，只要每个服务的代码仓库和部署流水线彼此独立就够了
一个分布式单体：既有单体的耦合又有分布式的开销，并不是真正微服务
questions.explanation: 书明确说「共享数据库的微服务」不是微服务：边界上下文要求数据也隔离，不允许多个服务共享集成数据库，否则改一张表又牵动所有服务。独立部署只解决了一半问题。
questions.question_en: A team splits its system into ten independently deployed services, but they share one database, so changing a table requires coordinating all of them. What does the book call this?
options_en: A sensible microservices compromise: the shared database ensures strong consistency while keeping independent deployment
An event-driven architecture that relies on database triggers to pass messages and state changes between services
Standard microservices architecture, as long as each service has its own code repository and deployment pipeline
A distributed monolith: it carries the monolith's coupling and the overhead of distribution, and isn't really microservices
questions.explanation_en: The book is explicit that “microservices sharing a database” aren't microservices: bounded contexts require data isolation and forbid shared integration databases, or changing one table ripples through every service. Independent deployment solves only half the problem.
